note: An additive overlay that records which workflow actually writes the committed data/latest_korea_market_signals.json pointer. It is deliberately NOT a ratification and NOT a policy: no threshold, status, authority or acceptance state anywhere in this repository changes because this file exists. config/regime_source_owner_registry_v2.json is not edited -- its exact bytes are hash-bound by config/crypto_paper_runtime_v1.json and config/kr_paper_runtime_ratification_candidate_v1.json (POLICY_BINDING_DRIFT on any byte change, at regime/crypto_paper_runtime.py and regime/kr_paper_runtime_ratification_candidate.py), and those files are in turn hash-bound by committed append-only evidence. This is the same separate-additional-record pattern config/paper_runtime_normalization_v1.json, config/regime_semantic_freshness_policy_v1.json and config/us_session_calendar_source_v1.json already use, and which the registry's own registry_binding reason field names.

The approval's intent, a record that matches where production actually happens, is satisfied by this overlay. The approval's stated route, editing the registry, is not taken, because the registry's bytes are hash-bound by two fail-closed runtimes and by committed append-only evidence -- which is the scale report the record's own cio_obligations required before acting.
